assertsOn: analyzer OUTPUT (published symbols and relationships), not tree shapes

D1.title: a published name is spelled with a C++ keyword
D1.contract: C++ has no identifier spelled with a keyword (ISO 14882 [lex.name]); such a name resolves to nothing for any consumer, at any extraction point.

D2.title: an extends edge names a base equal to its source
D2.contract: A class cannot inherit from itself, and the namespace qualifier is the whole information content of a C++ inheritance edge.

D3.title: more than one contains/references row for one (source, target) pair in one file
D3.contract: One edge per pair for the read/include shapes, where many sites express ONE fact. `calls` is deliberately EXCLUDED: two call sites are two facts, each with its own M59.A7 line_number.

D4.title: a declaration the grammar error-recovered is published under a name that is not the declaration's own
D4.contract: A declared name is not a type. When the recovery displaced the declarator, the name is in the adjacent ERROR (recoveredDeclaredName) or there is no readable name and nothing is published.

D5.title: a symbol is published with a FUNCTION as its owner, and is not a local class/struct/enum
D5.contract: C++ has no nested function definition, so a `function_definition` inside a body is a local direct-initialization — a variable, not a function.

D6.title: the analyzer's own source uses a regex
D6.contract: The regex census is the honesty artifact; the doc's claim of zero must be true, not asserted.

D7.title: a specifier's name arrives as a qualified_identifier, so the class publishes as `anonymous`
D7.contract: A class/struct may have a qualified name (an explicit specialization) and its LEAF is the name; an enum has NO qualified name in C++, so one in that slot is a C++23 [[=attr]] the recovery displaced, and the declared name is the identifier beside it. Publishing `anonymous` also collides with the analyzer's own no-name sentinel.

R1.title: REPORTED, not gated: a class/struct node that ends before the source's own brace balance
R1.contract: A tree-sitter-cpp 0.23.4 limitation on legal macro-heavy C++. The analyzer cannot invent a class node the grammar did not produce, so this is reported with its measured count rather than hidden or worked around.
